title: Image Formats & Responsive Images 📸
description: Choose the right file format and use `srcset` and `sizes` for responsive displays.

slides.title: Common Image Formats 🧪
slides.content:
# JPEG, PNG, GIF, SVG, WebP

- **JPEG** – great for photos, millions of colours, lossy compression.
- **PNG** – supports transparency, lossless, ideal for logos, icons.
- **GIF** – limited colours, supports simple animation (mostly replaced by video).
- **SVG** – vector format, scales infinitely, perfect for icons and illustrations.
- **WebP** – modern format by Google, smaller file sizes with good quality; widely supported now.

Choose based on content type. For photographs, JPEG or WebP. For graphics with transparency, PNG or SVG.

slides.title: Introducing Responsive Images 🖥️📱
slides.content: # One Size Doesn't Fit All A huge desktop image wastes bandwidth on a phone. HTML provides `srcset` and `sizes` to let the browser pick the best image. ```html ``` - `srcset` lists image files with their intrinsic width (`480w` means 480 pixels wide). - `sizes` tells the browser how wide the image will be displayed in different viewport conditions.

quizData.question: What is the main purpose of the `srcset` attribute?

options.text: To define the image's alt text
To provide multiple image sources for different screen resolutions/sizes

quizData.explanation: `srcset` gives the browser a choice of images based on pixel density or viewport width.
